v.why: Obvious view: convs compound along paths; but saturation means a second conv into the output node adds less when one already feeds it.
One might think removal costs the same whatever the edge held, but deleting the strongest op loses much more than deleting skip or pool, and parents holding it are strong, so the floor is far away.
A residual skip might be expected to buffer a weak op, but skip-on-edge-3 parents are strong, so the harmful pool has more accuracy to destroy.
Headroom would predict smaller gains in strong parents, but node 2 reaches the output only via edge 5, and when edge 5 is none edits to edge 1 do nothing, which dominates the contrast.
A disconnected node 1 might seem to make edge 5 more critical, but such parents are already weak, so floor effects shrink the harm of a pool.
Deep plus shallow convs might seem complementary, but a parent already holding the strongest op on an output edge has less headroom.
One might expect conv paths to stack, but strong parents near the accuracy ceiling gain less from another conv.
A strong deep path might be expected to mask a weak shortcut op, but strong parents lose more when the residual becomes a pool.
Replacing the strongest op with a pool degrades the whole downstream stack much more than replacing skip or none.
Edge 4 looks important as a conv path, but redundancy with a conv on edge 5 makes its removal nearly free.
